Book research should include reader-review evidence alongside primary-text reading, identifying practical difficulties, negative experiences, differences in usability, and criticisms that the author might not address. Reviews must be checked against the book, duplicates should not be counted as independent evidence, and self-selected reviews must not be mistaken for clinical outcome studies. Count as experiences only readers who say they tried the method; keep reviews of another edition, format, translation or book apart; and do not count publisher blurbs or endorsements as reader reviews. Say how many reviews were read and how they were chosen, or that none could be found, and complete the book research either way.
